Shower With Your Dad Simulator is a very simple game, but extremely fun and hilarious at the same time.

The game has several main modes and a bunch of secret modes that unlock over time, either randomly while playing or by performing certain actions. At first glance it looks very basic, but hunting for all the achievements and discovering easter eggs shows that there is actually more to it than you would expect.

Some achievements are quite challenging, such as surviving several minutes in one mode or up to 6 minutes in another. These require actual strategy, like learning the correct order of the kids' colors and then focusing on maintaining it. It was challenging but not insanely difficult, which made it a really fun experience.

I was also pleasantly surprised that the game still received small updates, fixes, and quality of life improvements even after many years. One funny achievement required me to stand under the shower in Soapico mode after turning it on. I literally just stood there, alt-tabbed and did other things until the achievement popped. It was silly but typical for this kinds of bizarre games.

Definitely a classic funny arcade like game I discovered years ago.

Recommended: Great short experience if you enjoy simple, challenging and absurdly funny games with hidden depth and funny achievements.

Ladies and gentlemen, scholars and arcade enthusiasts, allow me to discuss one of the greatest interactive achievements of modern civilization: Shower With Your Dad Simulator 2015: Do You Still Shower With Your Dad?

Yes. That is the title. Yes. It is art.

🎮 Gameplay: Fast, Frantic, Father-Finding Excellence

At its core, the game asks one simple question:

“Can you correctly identify your dad in a room full of dads at high speed?”

And let me tell you — this is the kind of high-stakes decision-making they train astronauts for.

You control one of three boys navigating a chaotic shower room filled with identical-looking grown men moving at increasingly concerning speeds. Your mission? Reunite with the correct father before time runs out and your dignity evaporates like steam on tile.

The mechanics are simple:

Move.

Identify.

Commit.

Hope.

But the difficulty ramps up faster than your heart rate when you realize you may have chosen… incorrectly.

It starts manageable. Calm. Civilized.

Then suddenly:

Dads are moving faster.

Your brain forgets how colors work.

Your reflexes enter panic mode.

You question every decision you’ve ever made.

It’s beautiful.

🧠 Deep Lore (Yes, Really)

You might think, “Surely this is just an arcade joke.”

WRONG.

This is a profound exploration of:

Childhood confusion in crowded public spaces.

The universal fear of losing sight of your parent.

The fragility of human pattern recognition under pressure.

The eternal philosophical question: “Is that my dad?”

The locker room becomes a metaphor. The steam represents uncertainty. The ticking timer symbolizes the passage of youth. The dads? Society.

Or maybe they’re just dads.

Either way, it’s layered.

🔥 Difficulty Curve: From “Haha” to “Help”

The difficulty progression is masterful.

Round 1:
“Oh this is cute.”

Round 5:
“Okay this is mildly intense.”

Round 12:
“I have transcended time. I am one with the dads.”

Round 20:
“I can see colors that do not exist.”

It achieves that sacred arcade quality:

Easy to understand.

Brutal to master.

Impossible to quit.

You fail, and instead of rage, you feel motivation. You whisper to yourself:
“I will find the correct dad next time.”

And you mean it.

🎨 Visuals: Pixelated Perfection

The pixel art is crisp, readable, and beautifully chaotic. Every dad is distinct enough to identify — until your brain melts and they all merge into one father-shaped blur.

The design prioritizes clarity, which is critical when you’re operating at 200 IQ dad-detection speed.

Minimalism? Yes.
Effective? Absolutely.
Steam physics? Emotionally accurate.

🎵 Audio: The Soundtrack of Destiny

The music is upbeat, frantic, and perfectly tuned to your rising stress levels. It feels like the soundtrack to a championship esports tournament, except the prize is paternal accuracy.

The sound effects provide feedback that gently says:

“Good job.”
Or
“That was not your dad.”

Powerful stuff.

🎯 Replayability: Infinite Dad Energy

Multiple game modes remix the formula in ways that keep things fresh. Leaderboards fuel your competitive spirit. You’ll say “one more round” approximately 47 times.

This is the kind of game you boot up for five minutes and emerge from an hour later, sweaty and victorious.

🏆 What Makes It Great (Scientific Breakdown)

A good game needs:

✔ Clear mechanics
✔ Responsive controls
✔ Escalating challenge
✔ Memorable identity
✔ Replayability
✔ Emotional resonance
✔ Dad density

This game has all of them.

It knows exactly what it is: absurd, focused, polished chaos.

There is no bloat. No filler. Just pure arcade precision wrapped in comedic brilliance.

🎓 Final Thoughts

Shower With Your Dad Simulator 2015 is more than a game.

It is:

A reflex trainer.

A psychological experiment.

A social commentary.

A dad-locating simulator.

A lifestyle.

It dares you to judge it by its title.
Then it outplays you.

Underneath the steam and silliness is a tightly designed arcade experience that respects your time, challenges your reflexes, and leaves you laughing while desperately sprinting toward the correct paternal figure.

I am really mixed about this review since I actually liked at first when one friend gifted it to me. A couple of years later I wanted to complete it... and the more I played it, the more I got frustrated with it. The jokes are funny and I liked the design and concept, simply the absurdity of the game title. But there are numerous things that make the game frustrating the more you play it.

I didn´t like the following things:

1. Unlocking game modes & randomness of those game modes:
I just don´t like that I have to play 501+ rounds of one of the main gamemodes to unlock the most challenging one. And the gamemode you unlock is the worst experience ever if you´re looking to get it without any help. There´s another gamemode that just didn´t unlock for me for ages and that frustrated me as well. There´s another point&click adventure gamemode where you have to fix a shower and the solution made 0 sense for me. Finding the real D.A.D was also a struggle.

2. Steam Achievements:
Be aware that if you don´t like Arcade games and you´re looking for an easy 100%, this is not the game you want. You have to be really clever and a pro gamer to get all the achievements without any help. I don´t mind it if an achievement is a challenging task, but idk.. "the man with the iron shower" and "finding the real D.A.D" are just way too hard.

3. The Man with the Iron Shower
You unlock this gamemode after grinding it out and I played this gamemode the most. It´s incredibly hard. The reason for me not recommending this game is this gamemode. You have to dodge 3, than 4, and 5 ninjas who are incredibly fast while the dad of those ninjas throws 1, and then up to 5 shurikens into your last direction every few seconds. You can´t touch any of those ninjas or shurikens. Simultaneously, one of the little ninjas stops for a brief moment and then jumps with a boost to your last position while all the other ninjas bounce off the walls. I don´t know if I encountered numerous bugs or if the gamemode is just so fast paced that the hitboxes do not properly work on the shurikens or ninjas. But its extremly frustrating. Many people talk about a glitch you can use to get into the walls so the little ninjas can´t hit you, but I think its intentionally made by the developer to help people that are struggling with the gamemode. I played this gamemode for hours, trying to get the achievement the legit way.

[h3]Conclusion:[/h3]
If you like to grind it out and play a really challenging arcade games just for fun and you´re looking for a low investment to expand your steam library, this game is for you. If you´re looking for a low priced game that you can easily complete to 100% all the achievements, I wouldn´t recommend buying it unless you feel the need to challenge yourself.

[hr][/hr][h1]Shower With Your Dad Simulator 2015 Do You Still Shower With Your Dad ✔️[/h1]
[hr][/hr][b]Shower With Your Dad Simulator 2015: Do You Still Shower With Your Dad — культовая сатирическая игра из 2015 года, которая в своё время гремела на каналах известных летсплейщиков. Её геймплей строится на серии режимных мини-игр, которые, пусть и кажутся однотипными, умудряются удерживать внимание за счёт своей абсурдной динамики.
[u]Понравилось:[/u]
● Геймплей. Вы — ребёнок, который ищет своего единственного отца среди нескольких голых мужчин в душе. Просто? Да. Но с появлением мыла, заявлений об опеке и прочих безумных предметов процесс становится на удивление азартным. Правда, до тех пор, пока не наступает пресыщение.
● Графика. Пиксельный стиль здесь не просто уместен — он отлично подчёркивает абсурд происходящего и добавляет иронии.
● Юмор. Если существует туалетный юмор, то в этой игре он скорее душевой... или душевный, кому как удобнее. Во вставках, встречающихся в переходах между режимами, часто проскакивают шутки, которые хоть и ориентированы на омэриканскую аудиторию, но вполне могут показаться забавными даже для живущих за пределами штатов людей.
● Звук. Музыка в игре задорная и незамысловатая, идеально подходит к жанру. Звуки не менее потрясны: соответствуют абсурдности происходящего на экране и, что важно, не режут слух.
● Цена. С учётом скидки игра обойдётся всего в ~21 рубль, что можно расценивать как вполне хороший прайс.
● Достижения. Их наличие — плюс, их получение — скорее минус, чем плюс. Платина даётся с большими усилиями, чего я, к сожалению, в этой игре не потянул.
● Коллекционные карточки. Приятный бонус для сообщества Steam: карточки можно продать или обменять, а предметы из магазина очков — использовать для украшения профиля.
[u]Не понравилось:[/u]
● Сюжет. В игре есть намёк на историю, но вникать в её запутанные хитросплетения — сомнительное занятие. Для полного понимания придётся пройти через хардкорные режимы и вымучить некоторые достижения.
● Сложность. Некоторые режимы откровенно мозговыносящие и требуют неоправданно много тренировочных заходов, что для игры такого формата выглядит избыточным.
● Гринд. Вытекающий из предыдущего пункт, так как и достижения, и игровая прогрессия требуют "закрытия" определённых критериев, данных на уровень, будь то 100 пойманных отцов или выжатое в скоростном режиме время.

A Surprisingly Brilliant Experience — Shower With Your Dad Simulator

I never expected a game with a title as outrageous as Shower With Your Dad Simulator to broaden my horizons as a gamer, yet here I am—writing a genuinely glowing review for one of the most unexpectedly charming and creatively bold indie games I’ve ever played.

The developers leaned hard into the humor, but they didn’t slack on the mechanics, and that combination makes the game surprisingly memorable.

The pixel art is charmingly minimalistic, and the absurd premise somehow only enhances its nostalgic vibe.

What really expanded my perspective, though, is the game’s unapologetic willingness to be weird. In a gaming landscape that often plays it safe, this title demonstrates how creativity can thrive when developers embrace the unconventional. It showed me that great gaming experiences don’t always need cinematic cutscenes, massive budgets, or complex narratives. Sometimes, all it takes is a brilliantly executed idea—no matter how off-the-wall it may seem.
